items.title: Airbus Receives Order For Two More Galileo Satellites
items.summary: The European Space Agency, on behalf of the EU Agency for the Space Programme and under a European Commission delegation, ordered two more Galileo satellites with stronger anti-jamming protection from Airbus.
paragraphs: The European Space Agency, on behalf of the EU Agency for the Space Programme and under a European Commission delegation, ordered two more Galileo satellites with stronger anti-jamming protection from Airbus. The pair adds to six second-generation satellites already on order and will use the same manufacturing capabilities, with work at Backnang, Friedrichshafen, Getafe, Ottobrunn and Toulouse. Each spacecraft is designed to weigh more than two tonnes, operate for 15 years and carry an enhanced atomic clock configuration and inter-satellite links for new signals and services.
Why it matters: The order adds two satellites to the six second-generation Galileo spacecraft Airbus already has on order, built across five European sites.

items.title: Poland Selected to Host New European PAC-3 Missile Maintenance Facility
items.summary: According to European Defence Review, Poland was selected as the host nation for the European Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Maintenance Facility.
paragraphs: According to European Defence Review, Poland was selected as the host nation for the European Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Maintenance Facility. Critical supply chain integration for the new facility will be led by Germany, the Netherlands, and Sweden, advancing commitments made under the NATO 3.0 framework. According to the announcement, the regional hub is intended to bring maintenance, repair and overhaul to Europe, shortening turnaround times and improving readiness.

items.summary: The U.S. Air Force plans a $1 billion facility at Nellis to test the F-47 sixth-generation fighter.
paragraphs: The U.S. Air Force plans a $1 billion facility at Nellis to test the F-47 sixth-generation fighter. The fiscal 2027 budget request includes $730 million for hangars and support infrastructure, and the schedule allows nine months for design and preconstruction following the initial award.

items.title: British Army plans to procure Heavy Wheeled Recovery Vehicle for Boxer
items.summary: The British Army plans to procure a Heavy Wheeled Recovery Vehicle to support Boxer vehicles on the battlefield.
paragraphs: The British Army plans to procure a Heavy Wheeled Recovery Vehicle to support Boxer vehicles on the battlefield. The vehicle order stands at 623 Boxer units, with over 500 built in the UK, alongside seventy-two Boxer RCH Artillery vehicles intended to replace the AS90. An armored recovery module from Flensburger Fahrzeugbau Gesellschaft was assessed and rejected for the role in favor of a generic heavy wheeled recovery vehicle.

Why it matters: The British Army is seeking a generic heavy wheeled recovery vehicle for its 623-strong Boxer fleet after rejecting a dedicated recovery module from Flensburger Fahrzeugbau Gesellschaft.

items.summary: Weibel will supply XENTA-M5 radars for Poland's SAN integrated counter-drone programme, with PIT-RADWAR serving as the customer under the contract.
paragraphs: Weibel will supply XENTA-M5 radars for Poland's SAN integrated counter-drone programme, with PIT-RADWAR serving as the customer under the contract. Weibel described the SAN programme as a step toward operational counter-drone capabilities on Europe's eastern flank.

items.summary: The United Kingdom has purchased sixteen Protector RG Mk1 air vehicles for the Royal Air Force, with eleven delivered into service and the remaining aircraft undergoing test and evaluation with the manufacturer, according to UK Defence Journal.
paragraphs: The United Kingdom has purchased sixteen Protector RG Mk1 air vehicles for the Royal Air Force, with eleven delivered into service and the remaining aircraft undergoing test and evaluation with the manufacturer, according to UK Defence Journal. items.title: Lockheed Martin showcases 1000 km PrSM Inc 4 prototype
items.summary: Lockheed Martin showcased its Precision Strike Missile Increment 4 prototype, which plans to use ramjet technology and an advanced sensor suite to strike moving ships and land targets over 1,000 kilometers away when fired from a HIMARS launcher.
paragraphs: Lockheed Martin showcased its Precision Strike Missile Increment 4 prototype, which plans to use ramjet technology and an advanced sensor suite to strike moving ships and land targets over 1,000 kilometers away when fired from a HIMARS launcher. The prototype submission plans to use a propulsion system from L3Harris and guidance systems informed by work from the company's Strigo Product Center. Lockheed Martin's current missile production line at Camden, Arkansas, can support the production of the Increment 4 offering, and the company is one of five firms selected by the U.S. Army to compete against submissions from Anduril, Castelion, Mach Industries and RTX, with tests in 2027 and 2028 informing the final award.
Why it matters: Lockheed Martin is utilizing its existing Camden production line for the PrSM Inc 4 offering to compete for the U.S. Army award alongside four other selected suppliers.
